fatal_errors: The proposed simultaneous-reduction mechanism is opposite to the reported sequential mechanism, in which Pt, Ir, or Ru reduces first, establishes a lattice, and catalyzes hydrogen-assisted reduction and incorporation of the remaining metals.
The asserted reduction-potential threshold of approximately 0.1 V has no cited or supplied evidentiary basis.
The proposed wet-chemical ligand-controlled synthesis does not reconstruct the spray-drying and hydrogen thermal decomposition-reduction route.

The hypothesis cannot explain the key Pt/Ir/Ru versus Pd comparison, which was attributed to differences in hydrogen adsorption, dissociation, and desorption rather than matched precursor reduction onsets.
explanation: The response addresses homogeneous multimetal alloy formation and proposes a testable comparison, so it has reasonable high-level problem alignment. However, it misses the central reported mechanism and conditions. Successful formation did not require simultaneous reduction: early reduction of Pt, Ir, or Ru was mechanistically beneficial because the newborn noble-metal lattice and reactive surface hydrogen promoted reduction and incorporation of Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe. The Pd and noble-metal-free controls are therefore especially damaging to the proposed account. The generated baseline is assumed rather than tied to the reported controls, and changing a ligand may alter coordination, adsorption, nucleation, and growth in addition to reduction onset, weakening causal discrimination. Its predicted single-phase and homogeneous products overlap only generically with the reported outcome and omit porous three-dimensional nanoframework formation, phase-dependent fcc/hcp behavior, and catalytic performance.
